program_plain: World: N identical oscillators, each coupled to every other (no space). Each has a voltage between 0 and 1, drawn uniformly at random at the start. Rules: (1) all voltages rise at the same constant speed (straight-line charging, no leak); (2) when a voltage reaches 1 the oscillator fires and resets to 0, together with any oscillators already firing with it as a group; (3) a firing group of k oscillators kicks every other voltage up by k/N; (4) any oscillator pushed to 1 or above by a kick joins the firing group and fires with it from then on. Run until the grouping stops changing and record whether all N end as one group. Sizes: N from 2 to about 100, many random starts per N (exact enumeration for N up to 8).
also_in_class_plain: Same rules with N prime (2, 3, 5, 7, 11): the only failure is all N staying separate.
Same rules with even N (4, 6, 8, ...): failures fall off only slowly with N.
Same rules with N divisible by 3 but not 2 (9, 15, ...).

observed.gloss: share of random starts ending as one group, N=4
share of random starts ending as one group, N=5
share of random starts ending as one group, N=6
number of possible final groupings at N=100, all equal-sized
failure probability falls as N to minus this, even N
prefactor of that failure power law for even N

program_plain: World: two continuous concentration fields u and v on a 128x128 square grid with wrap-around edges, started at their uniform steady state (u=b, v=b/(a+b^2)) plus small random noise. Rules, integrated forward in time: u changes at rate -u + a*v + u^2*v + D1*(Laplacian of u) + c1*div(u grad v); v changes at rate b - a*v - u^2*v + D2*(Laplacian of v) + c2*div(v grad u). The last terms make each species drift along the other's gradient, with strength and sign set by c1 and c2. Parameters: a=0.015, b=10, D1=0.01, D2=1000*D1. Main sweep: c1=c and c2=-c (opposite signs, so one species is drawn toward the other while the other is pushed away), c from 0.01 to about 0.5.
also_in_class_plain: Same rules with D1=0.1 and D2=100.
Same rules with b=5, D1=0.03 and c1=-c2 negative: spots turn into stripes, then fade, as |c| grows.
Same rules with c1=c2=c (equal signs).

observed.gloss: drift coupling c where the steady spot pattern is most intense
drift coupling c at which the pattern has vanished (uniform)
maxima of pattern amplitude as coupling increases (rise then fall)
spot-to-stripe morphology changes as coupling magnitude increases
independent random seeds reproducing the morphology sequence

program_plain: World: 1000 self-propelled disks (radius 1) in a periodic 2D box at area fraction 0.05, hovering at height 1.1 above a flat wall that chemicals cannot cross. Each disk emits a chemical. Rules each step: (1) each disk moves along its heading at speed 2; (2) it is pulled toward the others along the summed gradient of their screened chemical fields (each decays as exp(-k*r)/r, plus a mirror-image source below the wall), screening k between 0.18 and 0.22; (3) its heading is turned away from that same gradient with a positive turning strength (swept upward from 0); (4) the heading gets rotational noise (Peclet number 100); (5) disks repel on contact. A cluster is more than 10 disks linked within 2.1 radii.
also_in_class_plain: Same rules with screening 0.24-0.28: clusters burst open and the disks escape to a gas.
Same rules over a chemically permeable surface (no mirror source): only the bursting form, in a small window.

observed.gloss: time-averaged fraction of disks inside clusters
temporal fluctuation of the clustered fraction
neighbours per disk; stays below 5 (full collapse exceeds 5.6)
lower screening value of the cavity-filled cluster regime
upper screening value of the cavity-filled cluster regime
distinct collective states found across the parameter sweep

program_plain: World: 10,000 slightly elongated particles (ellipse half-axes 0.55 and 0.65) in a periodic 2D box at density 0.87 (lattice spacing about 1.15). Rules, overdamped Brownian dynamics at temperature T: (1) each pair interacts through an orientation-dependent Lennard-Jones potential of strength e_p (repulsive core, weak attraction, depending on both particles' orientations, which can rotate); (2) each pair also feels a non-conservative force with Lennard-Jones magnitude and strength e_a, directed perpendicular to the line joining them, always in the same rotational sense; (3) thermal noise acts on positions and orientations, orientations relaxing faster. Sweep the ratio e_a/e_p from 0 to 33 and T from 0 to 6; measure six-fold bond order and defect counts.

observed.gloss: force ratio e_a/e_p where solid is disordered even at T=0
force ratio e_a/e_p where crystalline order returns
temperature at which that high-activity solid stays ordered
temperature where the passive solid is only six-fold oriented

program_plain: World: a ring of 16,416 sites; between neighbouring sites is a bond tilted up or down (half of each, random), defining a height profile. Each site holds an A particle, a B particle or nothing (one third each, random). Rules, random sequential updates: (1) a particle swaps with a neighbouring site of different content; a move taking A downhill or B uphill succeeds with probability 0.9, the opposite move with 0.1; (2) a local peak (up-bond then down-bond) and a dip swap: a peak holding A becomes a dip with probability 0.5+b and back with 0.5-b, b=-0.4 (so A pushes ground up); a dip holding B becomes a peak with probability 0.5+b' and back with 0.5-b', b'=0.3; empty sites flip either way with 0.5. Track domain size over time.
also_in_class_plain: Same rules with b'=0.18 (late growth exponent about 0.41).

observed.gloss: power-law exponent of domain size growth before t~1000
power-law exponent of domain size growth at late times
time at which early domains dissolve and growth slows
macroscopic hills in the height profile in the late regime

program_plain: World: a 200x200 square lattice with wrap-around edges; each site holds a classical unit-length 3D spin (random start). Energy: sum over pairs of J_n times the dot product of the two spins, with nearest neighbours J1=-1 (aligning), diagonal neighbours J2=0.28 and straight next-next neighbours J3=0.14 (both anti-aligning). These values make the lowest-energy states planar helical spin textures whose wave vector can point anywhere on a nearly circular ring of radius 0.66. Rules: Metropolis Monte Carlo at temperature T, from the uncorrelated regime (T above 0.2) down to 0.02. Measure the local helix wave vector and helix-plane orientation, and count point defects as their windings around small loops (radius 3 sites).

observed.gloss: point defects per site in the correlated intermediate-temperature regime
density of defects winding only the helix-plane orientation
helix wave-vector rotation (in full turns) around the commonest defect
sharp specific-heat peak where lattice-rotation symmetry breaks
broad specific-heat hump where helical correlations begin

program_plain: World: an 800x800 square lattice with wrap-around edges; each site holds a continuous mass (mean 1 per site). Rules, repeated: (1) pick a random site and one of the four directions at random; (2) the site keeps 40% of its mass plus a random share of the rest and sends the remainder one step in that direction; (3) the receiving site pools it with its own mass, keeps 60% plus a random share of the rest, and passes the remainder one step to its left (a 90-degree counter-clockwise turn), so mass moves along L-shaped paths that always turn the same way. Rates are identical for all four directions and total mass is conserved. Measure steady-state density-density correlations and long-wavelength fluctuations.
also_in_class_plain: Same rules in a closed box with reflecting walls: a steady mass current circulates along the edges.

observed.gloss: density correlations decay as distance to minus this power
ratio of correlations along x and along y (isotropic)
optimal turning strengths minimising long-wavelength density fluctuations
square-root cusp exponent of fluctuations near maximal turning strength

program_plain: World: about 2.1 million dumbbells (two identical beads of diameter 1 joined by a stiff spring) in a square periodic 2D box at area fraction 0.65. Rules, Langevin dynamics with mass: (1) every pair of beads repels on contact (purely repulsive, no attraction); (2) each dumbbell feels a constant torque, equal and opposite forces perpendicular to its axis on its two beads, all spinning the same way, strength set by Peclet number 5 (swept); (3) beads have mass and weak friction (momentum persists; Prandtl number 0.005) plus thermal noise at temperature 0.01. Start homogeneous and watch the local density field.
also_in_class_plain: Other torque strengths above Peclet number about 1, at area fractions inside the coexistence window.

observed.gloss: torque strength above which the uniform state splits apart
exponent of domain size growth with time after splitting
coexisting states: dilute liquid and dense six-fold ordered state
global area fraction of the illustrated split state

program_plain: World: 40,500 rigid banana-shaped particles in a periodic 3D box at packing fraction 0.51; each particle is 16 beads of diameter 1 along a circular arc of length 15 and radius 10. Beads of different particles repel (purely repulsive Lennard-Jones). The particles start in the equilibrium phase where their bend directions rotate helically along one axis. Rules: molecular dynamics at temperature 1 while the box is sheared at constant rate 0.0001 (flow along x, varying with height z), with the helix axis pointing along the flow; shear to strain about 10. Coarse-grain particle orientations on a grid, locate line defects and measure their topological (skyrmion-type) charge.

observed.gloss: topological charge carried by the twisted defect lines
shear strain at which a tracked defect line forms
final angle (degrees) between helix axis and flow
shear strain reached when the system has reordered

program_plain: World: a large patch (384 rings of tiles) of the non-repeating single-tile tiling found in 2023 that needs no mirror-image tiles; each tile is a cell, neighbours are tiles sharing at least a corner. States 0, 1 and 3; all 0 except a seed of two adjacent tiles in states 1 and 3. Rules, synchronous, first matching rule applies: (1) a 0-cell with at least 3 neighbours in state 0 and at least 1 in state 1 becomes 3; (2) a 3-cell with at least 3 neighbours in state 3 becomes 0; (3) a 3-cell with at least 1 neighbour in state 1 becomes 1; (4) every other cell becomes 0. A window regenerates the tiling ahead of the active cells.
also_in_class_plain: Different four-state threshold rules on the companion 2023 single-tile tiling that uses mirrored tiles (three such rules found).

observed.gloss: rings of tiles crossed at constant speed without dying
rings of tiles advanced per generation
number of travel directions observed, 60 degrees apart
deviation of heading from nearest allowed direction, degrees
peak number of non-zero cells in each travelling object
share of two-tile seedings that launch travellers

program_plain: World: individuals at continuous positions in a square periodic domain, starting with 4,000 placed at random. Rules (continuous-time birth and death): (1) each individual gives birth at rate 1920; the offspring lands at a Gaussian offset (standard deviation 0.05); (2) each individual dies at rate 192 + (density of others within radius 1.25) + g times (density within radius 0.0625, squared: a three-body crowding term). Densities are counts divided by disk area. Only competitive (harmful) interactions, no attraction or help. Sweep g from 3.3e-6 to 3.9e-5 and look at the steady spatial pattern.
also_in_class_plain: Same rules with g = 2.35e-5 (spots stretching into stripes).
Death-to-birth ratio near 0.55: as g rises, spots, then stripes, then spots again.

observed.gloss: pattern anisotropy index jumps from 0 to this value
three-body strength where clusters form a hexagonal spot array
three-body strength where clusters merge into parallel stripes
three-body strength where empty holes sit in a populated background
death/birth ratio where spots reappear beyond the stripes

program_plain: World: an L x L square lattice with wrap-around edges (L up to 2048), each site holding a planar unit spin (an angle). Energy: minus the sum over all pairs of J(r) times the cosine of their angle difference, where every pair interacts with J(r) proportional to 1/r^4 (r = distance), normalised so that the total coupling per site is fixed. Rules: equilibrium Monte Carlo with cluster updates at inverse temperatures beta = 1, 2, 4, 8 and near the ordering point. Measure the squared magnetisation and the correlation length versus L.
also_in_class_plain: Nearest-neighbour coupling 1.2 plus a weak 1/r^4 tail: the tail still changes the low-temperature scaling.

observed.gloss: magnetisation decays as power of log L; exponent at beta=1
same exponent at beta=8 (proportional to temperature)
slope of squared correlation-length ratio versus log L, beta=1
2*pi times slope times exponent; 1 means spin-wave picture holds
power-law divergence exponent of correlation length at the transition

program_plain: World: 500 agents, each holding opinion +1 or -1, every agent able to interact with every other. Rules each step: pick an agent; with probability eta (around 0.002, the inverse population; swept) it flips its opinion at random; otherwise it copies the opinion of a randomly chosen other agent. Separately, at rate r (swept), a population-wide shock occurs: opinions are instantly reassigned so that the average opinion jumps to 0.3 (65% holding +1). Measure the long-run distribution of the average opinion.

observed.gloss: peaks in long-run distribution of the average opinion
average opinion at the extra, shock-induced peak
distinct long-run regimes across the noise-versus-shock-rate plane
noise level separating one-peak and two-peak behaviour without shocks

program_plain: World: a 2D surface exchanging particles with a reservoir (grand-canonical Monte Carlo; about 1,300 particles at close packing). Particles are hard elliptical disks with axis ratio 2 that cannot overlap; each carries two sticky patches, one at each tip of its long axis (patch half-angle 45 degrees, reach 0.17 particle diameters, bond energy -1), allowing up to two bonds per patch. Rules: Monte Carlo moves (single and cluster translations and rotations, insertions, deletions) at temperature T and chemical potential mu. Start from a dilute gas (density 0.004) quenched to T=0.145 with mu between -5 and 1 (full grid: T 0.055-0.16, mu -7 to 5). Track bonds and closed rings of bonded particles.
also_in_class_plain: Lower temperatures 0.07-0.115 at mu=-5: the same open lattice nucleates directly from the gas, with more defects.

observed.gloss: global order of six-particle rings (1 = perfect lattice of triangles)
fraction of particles belonging to closed rings
three-patch bonding triangles present after equilibration
peak count of two-patch pair bonds during nucleation, T=0.07
delay between rises of pair and triangle bond counts

program_plain: World: 10,000 point particles in a 100x100 periodic box (density 1), with no collisions. Rules: (1) each moves forward at constant speed 0.1 along its heading (small inertia); (2) it sees only particles within distance R (5 to 10) inside a vision cone of half-angle pi/8 around its heading; (3) it turns toward the positions of the visible particles, turning rate 3 times the average sine of the angle between its heading and the bearing to each (no copying of their headings); (4) its heading gets rotational noise of strength 0.08. Seeing is one-sided: being seen does not imply seeing back. Run 10 million steps of size 0.005.
also_in_class_plain: Same rules with vision half-angle pi/12.
Same rules with turning strength 1 (the state extends to wider vision angles).

observed.gloss: fractal dimension of particle pattern (1 = lines, 2 = uniform)
areas of empty voids scale as vision range to this power
number of particle streams meeting at the most common junction
largest junction degree seen; five or more essentially absent

program_plain: World: one closed loop of 2048 beads (a chain joined end to end) in open 3D space. Rules, Langevin dynamics with inertia: (1) consecutive beads are linked by springs and all beads repel at contact (no attraction), so the chain cannot cross itself; (2) each bead pushes itself with constant force along its own heading (activity: Peclet number Pe, swept); (3) headings diffuse randomly but with rotational inertia (reduced moment of inertia J swept 0.001-100, e.g. J=5); (4) beads have translational inertia (reduced mass M=0.3), friction and thermal noise. Measure loop size (radius of gyration) versus Pe, J and bead number.
also_in_class_plain: Same rules with J=30: very sharp switch back to an open coil within a narrow Pe window.
Same rules with J=10: compact loop size nearly independent of bead number.

observed.gloss: squared loop size shrinks by over this factor versus passive
Peclet number giving the most compact loop
Peclet number above which the loop swells back open
exponent of loop size versus bead number at J=10 (near zero)

program_plain: World: self-propelled point particles in a periodic 2D box (square of side 1200, or rectangular), density 1 per unit area. Rules, discrete time steps: (1) each particle sets its heading to the average heading of all particles within distance 1 (itself included), plus a uniformly random angle in [-eta*pi, eta*pi], with noise eta between 0.28 and 0.35; (2) it moves 0.5 along its new heading. Start from random positions and headings, or from alternating parallel strips of opposite headings. Run up to 10^8 steps and watch the dense travelling stripes that form.
also_in_class_plain: Continuous-time version (sine alignment plus Gaussian angular noise): same phenomenology.
eta=0.29, density 1, long rectangular box: very long lanes buckle and merge.

observed.gloss: side-by-side lanes of stripe trains travelling in opposite directions
share of random starts ending in opposite-travelling lanes (1 of 24)
lower noise of window where opposite-travelling lanes form
upper noise of window where opposite-travelling lanes form
time steps lanes persisted without disappearing

program_plain: World: a 100x100 square lattice with wrap-around edges of classical unit spins, all tilted slightly (within 0.2 rad) from the +z axis, coupled to one damped oscillator y(t). Rules: (1) y obeys y'' + gamma*y' + w0^2*y = white noise whose strength is set by a bath temperature (T/T0 = 1); oscillation period 0.001, coherence time 20 to 200 periods; (2) each spin precesses about its local field, whose x-component is g0*(1 - y) and z-component 5*(1 + y)*(sum of z-components of its 4 neighbours), with g0 set so spins turn by pi+0.001 per oscillator period. No external periodic drive. Record z-magnetisation once per period for 10,000 periods, 100 noise realisations.
also_in_class_plain: Coherence time 200 periods instead of 20 (sign reversals rarer).
Very long coherence (10^5 periods), period 0.2, T/T0 = 0.9: response stays doubled beyond 1000 periods.

observed.gloss: period of magnetisation divided by oscillator period
bath temperature (T0 units) sustaining doubling, long-coherence variant
bath temperature (T0 units) too weak for doubling, same variant
periods the doubled response survived in that variant, T/T0=0.9

program_plain: World: three continuous fields on a 50x50 periodic square: cell density b, an attractant a made by the cells, and a nutrient n eaten by the cells; all start uniform at 1 plus small noise. Rules (dimensionless): (1) b diffuses and drifts up the gradient of a with strength 5*b/(1+b^2) and up the gradient of n with strength 14*b/(1+b^2); cell number is conserved; (2) a diffuses 2.5 times faster than cells, is produced at rate b and decays at rate 1; (3) n diffuses 0.75 times as fast as cells, is consumed at rate 0.02*b*n and resupplied at rate 0.02 everywhere.

observed.gloss: kinds of structure coexisting: one dense blob and travelling bands
dense aggregates sitting in or carried by the bands
attractant/nutrient drift-strength ratio where this appears (5/14)

program_plain: World: a triangular lattice (6 neighbours per site) of linear size 100 with open edges; each site holds a director angle defined modulo 180 degrees. Rules, deterministic (zero noise): each site's angle changes at a rate equal to the sum over its 6 neighbours of w*sin(2*(neighbour angle - own angle)), where w = exp(s*cos(2*phi)) and phi is the angle between the bond to that neighbour and the site's own director, s from 0 to 0.5. A site thus listens more to neighbours lying along its own axis, so influence is not mutual. Start from imposed defect textures (single half-integer defects, or one integer +1 defect with texture phase mu); locate defects by angle winding around triangles.
also_in_class_plain: Continuum version with the corresponding extra torque term: isolated +1/2 defect speed rises with s.

observed.gloss: sign of change in +1/2 defect self-propulsion speed as s rises
intrinsic translation speed of isolated -1/2 defects
share of initial phases where +1 splits into four defects, s=0.5
same share at s=0.10
asymmetry strength s above which four-defect splitting appears
